text.text_excerpt: We had dinner here for the first time the other night. It was pretty good and we'll go back again soon I am sure. The only other Thai I have had in the city is at the Chill Out Cafe.I like the location and decor of Chill Out Cafe better, but I think I prefer the food at this place because they have a more expanded menu with some options not available at the other place. We had the Chicken Satay and it was delicious.Tender, juicy and full of flavor. I had Tofu and steamed veggies with Peanut Sauce and a side of sticky rice (I LOVE sticky rice!) and my partner had Thai Fried rice. We both enjoyed our food and have no complaints at all. I thought this place was very good. We were at the zoo earlier and came here for an early dinner. We ordered a couple of things and it was all pretty tasty. I really liked their coconut soup. It was flavored really well and delicious. We had panang curry with shrimp. I think I'm getting over shrimp, but I did enjoy the curry part. The spicy eggplant was really good. The pad thai was one of the best pad thais I'd had in a while. The thai iced tea was also very good. Service was excellent.

I want to start off by saying, this is my favorite place to get some Pad Thai! They never disappoint and their food is always consistent. I used to frequent this place when I was more in the area, but now it's kind of far and hard to get parking sometimes. You have the option of parking on the street (if any), parking in front of the restaurant (very slim chance), or parking in a gravel lot near the train tracks. This place has similar hours to other Thai restaurants with them closing during the "dead hour" between lunch and dinner.
